matched.set_b_axis: From self-protective sociability to socially deployed communion
matched.overlap_description: Both describe Oblonsky's shift from charm and self-protection toward using sociability more deliberately for mediation, reassurance, and social repair, without a radical moral transformation.

unique_to_a.axis: From self-indulgent social mastery to tactful relational mediation

unique_to_b.axis: From shallow guilt to limited practical conscience
From carefree self-image to aware but untroubled social pragmatist

matched.set_a_axis: From evasive husband to partial domestic ally
matched.set_b_axis: From guilty estrangement to restored domestic intimacy
matched.overlap_description: Both track the marriage from betrayal and rupture toward a compromised but real domestic reconciliation, with warmth and functioning restored but trust never fully healed.

matched.set_a_axis: From amused acquaintance to trusted mediator-friend
matched.set_b_axis: From amused acquaintance to trusted social mediator
matched.overlap_description: Both describe Levin as moving from a warm, lightly asymmetrical acquaintance into a trusted friend for whom Oblonsky becomes a tactful intermediary, host, and practical helper.

matched.set_a_axis: From awkward civility to strategic mediation
matched.set_b_axis: From social civility to strained pragmatic mediation
matched.overlap_description: Both see the Karenin relation as beginning in polite distance and ending in instrumental mediation over Anna's divorce, with increasing strain and little genuine intimacy.

matched.set_a_axis: From social familiarity to protective allegiance
matched.set_b_axis: From family convenience to loyal intermediary
matched.overlap_description: Both capture the Anna relation as evolving from family/social familiarity into active loyalty and protective mediation, especially around divorce and social legitimacy.

matched.set_a_axis: From amused acquaintance to loyal admiration
matched.set_b_axis: From casual admiration to socially strategic alignment
matched.overlap_description: Both describe Vronsky as moving from pleasant social acquaintance toward a more integrated, tactful, and loyal alignment within Oblonsky's social world.

unique_to_a.axis: From evasive husband to partial domestic ally
From social familiarity to protective allegiance
From amused acquaintance to loyal admiration

unique_to_b.axis: From guilty estrangement to restored domestic intimacy
From family convenience to loyal intermediary
From casual admiration to socially strategic alignment

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From self-protective sociability to socially deployed communion
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins as a self-protective, pleasure-seeking man whose warmth serves mainly to restore his own comfort, preserve appearances, and manage social equilibrium. His agency appears through charm, evasion, and practical control rather than moral independence.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends as a still self-protective but more consciously relational mediator who uses communion both sincerely and tactically to soothe others, preserve harmony, and keep social life moving. He remains fundamentally self-possessed, but his sociability is more openly in service of connection.

trajectory.position_description: He begins in shame and panic after the marital crisis, then quickly shifts into routine, jokes, and practical management. His warmth is real but mainly functions to avoid moral confrontation and restore order.
key_moments: Remembers Dolly's discovery and feels shame
Tries to use routine and Anna's arrival to restore composure
Confronts Dolly with pity but returns to practical arrangements

trajectory.position_description: He becomes more securely himself in offices, restaurants, and social gatherings. He handles people with tact and humor, but his communion remains a tool for comfort, deflection, and emotional self-protection.
key_moments: Acts effortlessly at work and with Levin
Uses dinner conversation to normalize marriage troubles
Is briefly shaken by the railway death, then returns to usefulness

trajectory.position_description: His relational energy turns more openly toward helping others, especially Anna and Levin. He becomes a social intermediary whose communion is sincere enough to matter, though still not morally transformative.
key_moments: Feels relief at Dolly's thaw
Moves through Anna's and Levin's social world as a connector
Helps create conditions for later meetings and reconciliations

trajectory.position_description: He settles into a durable pattern: socially buoyant, tactful, and comfort-seeking, with occasional embarrassment or concern but no deep inward revision. His agency remains practical, while his communion becomes more consciously deployed for social ease and mediation.
key_moments: Enjoys hunt, dinners, club life, and elections
Manages Anna's divorce negotiations and family logistics
Shows discomfort in religious and political settings but returns to mediation

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Oblonsky does not undergo a radical moral conversion. He moves from panic-driven self-protection into a more settled form of socially effective communion, with his warmth increasingly used to soothe, connect, and manage others while preserving his own ease.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From shallow guilt to limited practical conscience
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins with fragmented guilt: he knows he has caused harm, but his shame centers on embarrassment, inconvenience, and being caught rather than on the moral reality of betrayal.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends with a broader but still limited conscience: he can recognize others' suffering, manage difficult situations responsibly, and feel real concern, yet he does not fully internalize moral accountability or transform his conduct.

trajectory.position_description: He admits fault in a split way, effectively saying it is his fault and yet not fully his blame. He feels Dolly's pain, but his concern is still mostly about restoring comfort and avoiding humiliation.
key_moments: Names his fault while self-exculpating
Feels shame at Dolly's suffering and his own exposure
Wants the crisis to disappear rather than to repent

trajectory.position_description: He begins to treat suffering more seriously, especially through Anna's mediation and the railway death, but this seriousness is translated into action rather than inward moral reckoning.
key_moments: Is genuinely shaken by the railway accident
Uses Anna as a mediator for reconciliation
Feels the possibility that Dolly may not forgive him

trajectory.position_description: During Anna's divorce crisis, he shows sincere concern and persistence, but frames the problem as something to be solved by tact, pity, and arrangement. His conscience is active, yet procedural rather than transformative.
key_moments: Is shocked by Karenin's divorce announcement
Presses Karenin toward divorce out of sympathy for Anna
Feels moved by Karenin's self-sacrifice but turns it into practical success

trajectory.position_description: Under financial and social pressure, he becomes more visibly self-protective and evasive again, but he also continues to act as a practical intermediary. His conscience remains real, yet subordinated to convenience, status, and administrative resolution.
key_moments: Feels humiliation and money pressure
Negotiates Anna's divorce through telegrams and visits
Withdraws emotionally when Anna's distress becomes too direct

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Oblonsky's moral development is modest but real: he never becomes deeply repentant, yet he moves beyond pure embarrassment into a limited practical conscience that can register suffering and act to relieve it. The arc is one of expanded usefulness rather than full ethical conversion.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From carefree self-image to aware social pragmatist
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins with a self-image of being naturally charming, harmless, and socially gifted, with little awareness of how much his ease depends on evasion, privilege, and other people's labor.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends with a clearer recognition that social life is structured by influence, money, and arrangement, though he remains comfortable inside that system and does not fundamentally question it.

trajectory.position_description: He experiences himself as a man who belongs effortlessly in offices, restaurants, and salons. He is aware of his own charm, but not of its costs or moral implications.
key_moments: Enjoys office life and dinner conversation
Speaks of marriage and infidelity in pragmatic terms
Uses wit to avoid spiritual seriousness

trajectory.position_description: He becomes more explicitly a connector among people, reading social situations quickly and using them to his advantage. He still sees this as natural competence rather than as a form of power.
key_moments: Shifts sympathy between Levin and Vronsky
Uses Anna and Dolly as mediators in domestic crisis
Feels relief when reconciliation seems possible

trajectory.position_description: In elections, appointments, and Petersburg society, he shows a sharper sense that status, influence, and networks determine outcomes. He is not morally transformed by this insight; he simply becomes more adept at operating within it.
key_moments: Navigates political maneuvering and committee appointments
Seeks help from powerful social and religious figures
Feels discomfort in unfamiliar ideological settings but still pursues advantage

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Oblonsky's self-understanding becomes more socially realistic over time: he increasingly sees life as a field of arrangements, favors, and tactful management. This does not make him more ethical, but it does make him more conscious of the mechanisms by which he thrives.

relational_axes.axis_name: From guilty estrangement to restored domestic intimacy
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins in guilt, fear, and emotional distance, with Dolly experienced as the injured moral center of the household and forgiveness seeming uncertain.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends in a restored but fragile intimacy: he is reconciled with her, affectionate and relieved, though still careful and aware that the wound has not vanished.

trajectory.position_description: He is ashamed, cornered, and emotionally shaken by Dolly's refusal to forgive him. Their intimacy remains domestic but trust is badly damaged.
key_moments: Dolly discovers the affair
He feels her suffering and fears losing her
She rejects his appeals and he feels bewildered

trajectory.position_description: Anna helps soften the atmosphere, and Dolly's use of his familiar name signals that reconciliation is possible. He becomes hopeful and relieved as the domestic crisis eases.
key_moments: Anna intervenes as mediator
Dolly calls him 'Stiva'
He feels reconciliation is again thinkable

trajectory.position_description: Their relationship is no longer the site of acute crisis. He treats her with warmth and familiarity, but the bond is maintained through tact, routine, and practical cooperation rather than innocence.
key_moments: He greets her warmly in social and domestic scenes
They coordinate wedding logistics and household arrangements
He remains affectionate but not deeply self-reforming

trajectory.position_description: Their relationship settles into a durable, if compromised, family intimacy. He remains dependent on her practical competence and social goodwill, while she continues to bear much of the emotional and domestic burden.
key_moments: Approves of the family summer arrangement
Uses her as a practical and social anchor
Is still associated with her through debts, messages, and family mediation

relational_axes.evidence_summary: The Dolly relationship is the clearest arc in Oblonsky's novel: from acute marital rupture to a managed, affectionate, and socially functional intimacy. Trust never returns to innocence, but domestic closeness is restored through tact and habit.

relational_axes.axis_name: From amused acquaintance to trusted social mediator
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as a warm but lightly superior acquaintance, amused by Levin's seriousness and awkwardness, with little sense that he will become emotionally important to Levin.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as a trusted, affectionate, and tactically useful friend who repeatedly mediates Levin's emotional life, helps him socially, and is treated as a reliable companion.

trajectory.position_description: He likes Levin and enjoys his company, but treats him as earnest, awkward, and somewhat odd. Their bond is warm but asymmetrical.
key_moments: Receives Levin warmly at the office and restaurant
Teases him gently about Kitty and marriage
Uses social tact to keep Levin comfortable

trajectory.position_description: He becomes a genuine social bridge between Levin and the Shtcherbatskys, and later between Levin and Anna. His sympathy is flexible, but his role as mediator becomes central.
key_moments: Shares gossip and matchmaking intelligence
Helps Levin navigate Kitty's situation
Brings Levin into contact with Anna and other social circles

trajectory.position_description: He is now a dependable friend in practical and emotional matters, helping with the forest sale, wedding logistics, and social introductions. Levin trusts him even when he disagrees with him.
key_moments: Hunts and dines with Levin
Argues lightly over the forest sale
Supports Levin through wedding preparations and ceremony

trajectory.position_description: He remains a warm, tactful, and socially stabilizing presence in Levin's life, even when Levin is jealous or morally serious. Their bond is durable, affectionate, and practically important.
key_moments: Hosts Levin at the country house and shooting trip
Responds to Levin's jealousy with tact and humor
Brings Levin to Anna and helps soften his judgment

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Levin is one of the few characters with whom Oblonsky develops a sustained, meaningful bond. The relationship deepens from amused familiarity into a trusted friendship in which Oblonsky repeatedly acts as mediator, host, and social translator.

relational_axes.axis_name: From family convenience to loyal intermediary
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as a family relation of convenience and social familiarity, with Anna initially serving as a possible mediator in his own domestic crisis.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as a loyal, practical ally who works to secure her divorce, protect her dignity, and help normalize her social position, though still through tact rather than moral depth.

trajectory.position_description: He greets her arrival with hope, seeing her as a possible mediator in his marital trouble. She is family support and social help before she becomes his cause.
key_moments: Anna arrives as a possible reconciler with Dolly
He feels relief and hope at her presence
She helps soften the domestic atmosphere

trajectory.position_description: He comes to rely on Anna as a sympathetic interpreter of his own domestic situation. Their relationship becomes warmer and more emotionally trusting.
key_moments: He is grateful for her intervention with Dolly
He trusts her as a family mediator
He feels relief when reconciliation is possible

trajectory.position_description: He shifts decisively into the role of Anna's defender and negotiator. He is shocked by Karenin's divorce announcement and then works actively to secure a practical settlement for Anna.
key_moments: Presses Karenin to consider divorce
Speaks of Anna with admiration and loyalty
Acts as messenger and facilitator of the settlement

trajectory.position_description: Even when the situation becomes more difficult and emotionally cold, he remains a practical intermediary. His loyalty persists, though it is increasingly filtered through administrative action and social convenience.
key_moments: Sends telegrams about the divorce
Continues to manage the legal and social process
Keeps Anna's interests in view while avoiding direct emotional confrontation

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Oblonsky's relation to Anna evolves from family familiarity into active loyalty. He never becomes a tragic participant, but he does become a dependable intermediary who helps her navigate divorce and social legitimacy.

relational_axes.axis_name: From social civility to strained pragmatic mediation
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins with ordinary social civility and a willingness to smooth over awkwardness, but with little real intimacy or trust.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends in a strained, instrumental relationship marked by tactical politeness, moral discomfort, and practical negotiation over Anna's divorce.

trajectory.position_description: He greets Karenin with habitual ironic civility, keeping the interaction smooth but emotionally shallow.
key_moments: Polite, sarcastic greeting
Maintains formal marital and social distance
Keeps the encounter within social propriety

trajectory.position_description: Karenin's divorce announcement shocks him, but he quickly shifts into mediation mode, trying to persuade him toward a practical settlement.
key_moments: Is startled by Karenin's announcement
Appeals to Dolly and Christian duty
Presses for divorce as the humane solution

trajectory.position_description: He becomes increasingly uneasy and detached in Karenin's religious circle, then more administratively focused as the divorce process continues. The relationship is now defined by procedure and discomfort rather than social ease.
key_moments: Feels alienated in Lidia Ivanovna's salon
Learns Karenin's refusal has been fixed by influence
Continues to manage the divorce through messages and errands

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Karenin is never a close relation, but he becomes a major practical and moral counterpart in Oblonsky's life. The relationship moves from polite distance to strained mediation, with Oblonsky repeatedly trying to convert conflict into a workable arrangement.

relational_axes.axis_name: From casual admiration to socially strategic alignment
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as a friendly acquaintance admired for charm and status, but not yet central to Oblonsky's social maneuvering.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as a socially useful and strategically aligned figure within Oblonsky's network, especially in the Anna/divorce and elite society contexts.

trajectory.position_description: He sees Vronsky as handsome, rich, and socially impressive, and he is pleased by his company. The relation is warm but still mostly social.
key_moments: Speaks of Vronsky with admiration
Enjoys his generosity and presence
Uses him as part of the social field around Kitty and Anna

trajectory.position_description: As Anna's situation becomes central, Vronsky becomes part of the practical social arrangement Oblonsky is helping to manage. He treats him as a legitimate and increasingly important participant.
key_moments: Greets Vronsky cordially
Supports the social normalization of Anna and Vronsky
Helps move toward the divorce settlement

trajectory.position_description: In later political and social scenes, Vronsky is simply one of the elite men with whom Oblonsky moves comfortably. Their relationship is easy, tactful, and socially coordinated.
key_moments: Shares race-course and club sociability
Moves in the same Petersburg circles
Treats Vronsky as part of the accepted social order

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Vronsky becomes less a romantic rival or scandalous figure than a socially integrated acquaintance. Oblonsky's relation to him is marked by tactful approval and practical alignment, especially once Anna's future depends on social arrangement.
